turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Happy to! Here is a worked example first.
Start: "I work in a shop." Change the subject to "he".
"He" is one person, so I add -s to the verb: "He works in a shop."
In short: when the subject is he, she or it, the verb ends in -s.
Right: She walks to the station every morning. Wrong: She walk to the station every morning.

Now it's your turn. Fill the gap with only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
